components.basis: Definition entry, no proof promised. Lines 21-45 give n!, 0!, binomial coefficients with value zero outside 0<=k<=n, natural logarithms, the meaning of ~, independent fair signs with S_N and lattice L_N (Durrett p. 113: i.i.d. +-1 steps, S_n, P(S_2n=2k)=C(2n,n+k)2^-2n for all integers via the zero convention), the binomial count B_N for fixed p in [0,1] (Feller's binomial), phi and Phi, ceiling/floor and the empty-supremum convention. The Gaussian normalization it invokes is proved on route before this chapter (convolution-gamma-normal.tex 301-312).

Annex 12-17 proves |log(1+t)-t|<=t^2 on |t|<=1/2; 18-30 proves the odd logarithmic series by integrating the finite geometric identity with a vanishing remainder; 32-39 proves the scalar limit, which is Durrett Lemma 3.1.1 (p. 114: c_j->0, a_j->inf, a_j c_j->lambda); 40-49 proves the triangular product limit under all three hypotheses of Durrett Exercise 3.1.1 (p. 115). The series is supplied on 0<y<1, the range in which Feller II.9 uses (8.11) at y=1/(2n+1) (p. 53, (9.9)).

Compared with Feller VI.3 pp. 150-151 and VII.1 pp. 175, 179. Annex 55-62: mass, normalization, mean, variance. 64-75: the ratio (3.1) and geometric comparison give (3.4) for r>Np, including r=N. 76-83: masses nonincreasing from ceil(Np), more than r-Np terms each >= b(r), giving (3.5). 84-88: failures give (3.6) for r<Np. 90-108: Lemma 2, (1.7) and the strict two-sided bound (1.8) for every x>0, proved by the derivative inequalities (1.9) of p. 179 and integration to infinity.

components.gap: Feller II.9 (pp. 52-54) is supplied only in its mathematics; its attributions and justificatory claims are absent from the route: (a) n. 14, the formula is James Stirling's, Methodus differentialis (1730); (b) n. 15, the d_n-difference argument and inequality (9.14) are due to H. E. Robbins, Amer. Math. Monthly 62 (1955) 26-29 - the route has only the label 'Robbins bounds' (body 101, 120; annex 112, 297, 717), with no attribution of the argument and no reference; (c) n. 16, the usual proof that e^C = sqrt(2 pi) rests on Wallis's formula, with Feller's direct proof in Amer. Math. Monthly (1967) - the cosine-integral determination (annex 245-253) is not identified with that route; (d) p. 53, the constant's proof is elementary, independent of chapters IV-VI, and postponed to VII.2 because it is naturally connected with the normal approximation theorem (neither stated nor reconciled with the argument's use of the VI.3 tail estimate); (e) pp. 52-53, the motivation of d_n as the simplest quantity close to the arithmetic mean of the two extremes of (9.5); (f) p. 54, after (9.15), the ratio of its extreme members is close to 1 - 1/(12 n^2), so the right-hand member overestimates n! by less than a fixed multiple of n^-2 per cent. Items (a)-(c) and (f) are written only in handbook/parts/p15/distributions-transforms-and-moment-problems-w02c-p15-011.tex, which no driver inputs (off route).
components.basis: Mathematics complete and checked step by step against Feller II.9 pp. 52-54 and VII.2 pp. 179-181: (9.3)-(9.5) annex 115-122; d_n and (9.7)-(9.10) 123-145; finite limit C 146-148; (9.13)-(9.14) 149-164 ((12n+1)(12n+13)-36(2n+1)^2=24n-23); unnormalized formula 165-169; the VII.2 n.3 constant argument with an unknown constant, the central ratio (2.2)-(2.7), the VI,(3.5) tail with 4/R^2 and the bound (1.8), 171-243; the independent cosine-integral determination 245-253 resting on weak-convergence-of-laws.tex 330-354 and its annex 572-634 (on route, input earlier); the n.17 refinement strengthened to |r_n-1/(12n)+1/(360n^3)|<=6/(5n^5), 255-297 (expansion coefficients, the identity for (3+3x+x^2)/(1+x)^3 and the 61/360 and 1/3 remainders verified). The gap is Feller II.9's non-proof content.

Annex 303-316: counting and exact Stirling give Durrett's (3.1.2) factorization with remainder e^{R_{n,k}} and the H(u) form; 317-330: Durrett's three-factor split (p. 114) and its limits, also for k<=0, giving Theorem 3.1.2; 332-364: H(0)=H'(0)=0, H''=2/(1-u^2), 0<=H-u^2<=2u^4/9, the log and |R|<=3/(8n) bounds, n>=2A^2 => |u|<=1/2, giving K_A/n; 366-383: odd parity by the last-sign step with the explicit argument shift; 384-386: wrong parity zero, extreme points 2^-N, no r_0.

components.gap: Durrett's remark after Theorem 3.1.3 (p. 115) that the result is a special case of the central limit theorem of Section 3.4 - his stated reason for leaving the details to the reader - and the chapter's opening statement (p. 113) that it begins with special cases of the central limit theorems that can be treated by elementary computations are not stated anywhere on the route (body 163-189 and annex 390-454 give the full proof but not this relation; body 348-349 only names the general CLT as a later presentation). The only statement of it is handbook/parts/p15/distributions-transforms-and-moment-problems-w02c-p15-011.tex lines 164-168, which no driver inputs.
components.basis: Proof complete: exact indices 392-397; Riemann sums with uniform local error (Durrett p. 114 summation) 399-416; the even-limit/odd-step route of Durrett's parenthetical S_{2n+1}=S_{2n}+-1 (p. 115) 418-440; strict and singleton endpoints, CDF and infinite endpoints 442-452. Definition entry, no proof promised: Poisson law for lambda>0 and lambda=0; X_i independent Poisson(1), i.e. Durrett's i.i.d. Poisson mean-1 summands of Exercises 3.1.2 and 3.1.4 (p. 115, P(X_i=k)=e^-1/k!); T_n kept separate from S_N.

Annex 458-466: normalization via the Taylor remainder e^lambda lambda^(m+1)/(m+1)! -> 0; 466-474: mean, factorial moment, variance, lambda=0; 476-491: the multinomial count gives P(T_n=k)=e^-n n^k/k!, Durrett's Exercise 3.1.2 premise; nonnegative integer summands give zero mass at negative integers.

Annex 497-503: exact form with J(u) and r_k; 504-518: |J-u^2/2|<=(2/3)|u|^3, |log(1+u)|<=2|u|, r_k<1/(6n), giving the uniform bound; 519-523: the moving-k limit sqrt(2 pi n)P(T_n=k)->exp(-x^2/2) of Durrett Exercise 3.1.2; 525-543: the interval consequence Durrett states but excludes from the exercise, with exact thresholds, Chebyshev cutoffs, strict, singleton and infinite endpoints.
Definition entry, no proof promised: gamma on [-1,1] with 0 log 0 = 0 (Durrett Exercise 3.1.3's gamma), I(a)=a log a - a + 1 for a>0 (Exercise 3.1.4's limit is -I(a)), log 0 = -inf.

Annex 549-565: k_n=ceil(na), exact factorization at u_n, limit -gamma(a); 567-578: ratio (n-k)/(n+k+1)<=(1-a)/(1+a) and the geometric comparison, following Durrett's hint (p. 115: P(S_n>=k)<=C P(S_n=k)); 580-589: a<=0, a=1, a>1. Durrett Exercise 3.1.3 for a in (0,1) is supplied.

Annex 595-603: point-mass rate a-1-a log a; 604-613: ratio n/(k+1)<=1/a and the geometric factor (1-1/a)^-1; 615-624: a=1 via P(T_n=n), 0<a<1 via Chebyshev, a<=0 surely. Durrett Exercise 3.1.4 for a>1 is supplied.

Annex 630-670: exact D(t||p) form, Taylor bound with M_p, uniform local limit; 674-685: Riemann sums, exact indices, Chebyshev cutoffs, convergence in distribution; 686-689: p=0,1.
